result.rule: When the description states that one party performs two activities joined by 'and', with no stated order between them, and both must be finished before the next described step: Model the two activities as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before them, connect each activity to a parallel gateway join, and continue from the join to the next step. Do not sequence the activities one after the other unless the description orders them, and do not put an exclusive gateway between them.

When the description says several activities are performed independently of each other and all of them must be completed before a later step can begin: Model a parallel gateway that splits the flow into one branch per independent activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches so the later step starts only after all of them finish. Do not leave the branches unsynchronized, and do not use an exclusive gateway for a join that requires every branch.

When the description states that an activity runs over a period, that one or more other activities run at the same time while it runs, and that a later step starts only after the period has ended and all of these concurrent activities have finished: Model the concurrent block as parallel branches: place a parallel gateway split before the running activity and the monitoring activity. Model the end of the period as an intermediate catch event (a timer or wait) that is also a branch of the concurrent block. Connect the monitoring activity and the period-end event to a parallel gateway join, so that no branch ends on its own or bypasses the join. Continue from that join to the later step. Do not use an exclusive gateway to merge these branches.

When the description states that an activity may also be performed as an optional extra step, on top of the main path, so it is not performed in every case (signalled by wording such as 'may also'): Place an exclusive gateway on the path at the point where the optional activity could occur. Give the optional activity its own outgoing sequence flow from that gateway, and give a bypass flow that skips it. Merge the optional branch and the bypass with an exclusive gateway before the next described step. Keep the required activities on the main path unconditional and do not drop the optional activity.
